resources.string: A recorder can keep today\'s encrypted traffic and wait. Once a large quantum computer exists, Shor\'s algorithm turns every recorded X25519 public key into its private key. PQXDH also runs ML-KEM-1024, which has no such known attack, and mixes its secret into the session key.
Record a chat over X3DH and one over PQXDH
Years later: break every X25519 key
%1$s · prekey bundle in bytes: %2$d · first message header in bytes: %3$d
The session key is rebuilt from them alone
The ML-KEM secret is still missing, so the session key cannot be rebuilt
Simulation: no quantum computer is involved. The attacker is handed the Diffie-Hellman outputs, which is what breaking the recorded X25519 keys would give.
User 2 publishes signed one-time ML-KEM prekeys and one signed last-resort key. Each new chat uses up a one-time key. When they run out, the last-resort key is used and kept.
